angle: AI value shows up only when you wire pilots to a P&L, not a slide deck.
sourceTitle: The state of AI in 2026: On the road to ROI
linkedinPost:
Enterprises don’t have an AI problem — they have a value plumbing problem.

A recent McKinsey piece argues we’re “on the road to ROI.” I see the same: agentic coding tools are saving time, and individual use is high. But many orgs still can’t show where AI hits the P&L.

From the front lines, the pattern is consistent. Pilots are optimized for demos, not deployment. Costs are tracked; benefits are assumed. And the data, security, and workflow handoffs needed to make value repeatable arrive last — or never.

What works instead:
- Start with a value hypothesis tied to a single metric (e.g., AHT -12%).
- Baseline it before you build. No baseline, no pilot.
- Put a product owner on the hook for adoption, not just model accuracy.
- Fund the “boring” layer: data quality, orchestration, observability, and AI FinOps.
- Ship to production in 90 days or kill it. Demos don’t compound; deployments do.

My take: if the pilot doesn’t have a measurable line to revenue, cost, or risk in month one, it’s theater. Treat AI like any other operating investment.

What’s your rule for greenlighting (or killing) an AI initiative? #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI #AIStrategy #AIAdoption
